Material data: the six presets are textbook values at 20 degrees (copper is the IACS figure, aluminium a commercial grade), and real conductors vary with purity, temper, alloy and drawing; the linear temperature coefficient is a fit near room temperature, not a physical law, and no alloy-specific or low-temperature behaviour is modelled.

Whether the resistance was measured with a method that excludes lead and contact resistance (a four-wire measurement), the accuracy of the measured length, section and resistance, and the heating of the sample by the measuring current: a resistivity found from a measurement carries all of those errors.

checked: Two linear, magnetically coupled coils with constant inductances at one frequency and current level. The self-inductances are entered or found from the turns on one closed core of constant relative permeability (L = N² / ℜ, ℜ = lc / (μ₀ μr Ac), μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m), and the coupling is given as a coefficient k, as a mutual inductance M, or from a series-aiding and a series-opposing measurement (M = (La − Lo) / 4).

The mutual inductance and coupling coefficient (M = k √(L1 L2), k ≤ 1), the inductance of the pair in series aiding and opposing and in parallel aiding and opposing (with the 0 / 0 limit for k = 1 and L1 = L2), the leakage inductance seen with the other coil shorted, L (1 − k²), the T-equivalent arms L1 − M and L2 − M, the flux linkages, the stored energy ½ L1 i1² + ½ L2 i2² + M i1 i2, the reactances at the frequency entered and the voltages induced for a given rate of change of coil 1 current.

Rejections of a mutual inductance (entered, or implied by the series readings) larger than √(L1 L2), of a series-opposing reading larger than the series-aiding reading and of a coupling coefficient outside 0 to 1; warnings when the two series readings do not average to L1 + L2 (more than 5% apart) and, with turns on a core, when the core flux density is above 1.6 T.
notChecked: Winding resistance, turn-to-turn and inter-winding capacitance, self-resonance, skin and proximity effect and core loss: the coils are ideal inductances and the results are not valid near or above the self-resonant frequency of a real coil.

The prediction of k or M from the geometry of air-core coils (coil spacing, diameters, alignment), the Nagaoka correction for a finite solenoid, an air gap, a core of several limbs and the saturation curve of the iron: with turns on a core the coupling is the k you enter, and a constant relative permeability is assumed.

Non-linear or frequency-dependent inductance, the sign of M for a particular winding direction and dot marking (M is taken as a positive size, and aiding and opposing are named for the connections), and the measurement uncertainty of an LCR meter: a result found from the series readings carries the errors of those readings.

checked: A three-phase cage induction motor on a balanced sinusoidal supply driving one machine at constant speed through a drive of constant efficiency: the power at the load shaft, the speed ratio and efficiency of the drive, a design margin, a derating factor, the rated speed, locked-rotor, average accelerating and breakdown torque ratios, the terminal voltage at start and while running, the breakaway and average accelerating load torque, the peak running load, the required torque margin, the two inertias, and the supply voltage, efficiency and power factor at the operating load.

The power the motor must deliver Pl / ηt, the design power with the margin, the nameplate rating needed after the derating factor, the smallest rating at or above it in the IEC 60072 preferred list (0.18 kW to 1,000 kW), the loading against the rating and against the derated output, the spare power, and the next smaller size with its loading for comparison.

The load torque at the load shaft and at the motor shaft, the rated torque of the chosen size, the starting torque kLR Tn (Vs / V)² against the breakaway torque of the load, the breakdown torque kbd Tn (Vr / V)² against the peak running torque, the total inertia at the motor shaft, the average accelerating torque and the time to full speed Jt ω / Tacc, and the input power, line current and reactive power at the operating load from the efficiency and power factor entered.

Warnings for a starting torque that does not exceed, or is less than the margin required over, the breakaway torque; a breakdown torque that does not exceed, or is less than the margin over, the peak running torque; no accelerating torque; an acceleration time above about 10 s; a loading of the derated output below 40%; a start voltage below 80%; and a need above the largest listed rating. Rejections of a need above 1,000 kW and of ranges outside the shared limits (a derating factor from 0.3 to 1, a drive efficiency above 0 and up to 100%, a start or running voltage above 0 and up to 120%, a peak load of 1 to 5 times normal).
notChecked: Any rule of a standard or a motor maker for selecting a motor: no sizing rule, service factor practice, duty-type (S1 to S10) derating or efficiency class of IEC 60034-1, IEC 60034-30-1 or NEMA MG 1 is applied; the margin, derating factor and torque margin are the user's figures and the size list is the preferred output series, not a catalogue.

The enclosure, insulation class, temperature rise, ambient and altitude derating (the derating factor is entered), cooling, protection, starter, drive and cable that follow from the choice, motors on a variable-frequency drive, synchronous, single-phase and wound-rotor motors, and duty with frequent starts, braking or reversing (no thermal check of the starts per hour or of the locked-rotor withstand time).

The full torque-speed and load-torque curves: the acceleration time uses one constant average torque for the motor and one for the load, the torque is taken as proportional to the voltage squared, the efficiency and power factor are the user's figures at the loading and are not changed with the size, and the rated speed and the torque ratios are taken as the same for the size chosen and its neighbours.

checked: A three-phase induction motor on a balanced sinusoidal supply, with the nameplate figures taken at rated output, rated voltage and rated frequency: output P, line voltage V, frequency f, poles, rated speed N, rated current In, power factor cos φ, efficiency η, service factor SF, the locked-rotor current ratio ILR / In and the winding connection.

The synchronous speed 120 f / p, the slip (Ns − N) / Ns, the slip speed and the rotor frequency s f, the rated torque P / ω, the input power P / η and the losses, the apparent and reactive power √3 V In and √3 V In sin φ, the winding voltage and current for a star or a delta winding, the locked-rotor current klr In and the continuous output SF P with its torque at the rated speed.
A consistency check of the plate: the current P / (√3 V η cos φ) against the plate current and the efficiency that the plate current implies, flagged when they differ by more than 5%.

Supply checks against the plate: the supply voltage and frequency deviation, the volts-per-hertz ratio against rated, the synchronous speed at the supply frequency, the current for the rated output at the supply voltage (In V / Vs, constant output) and a loading estimate from a measured current Im / In. Warnings for a rated slip outside 0.5% to 8%, a supply voltage more than 10% from rated, a supply frequency more than 5% from rated, volts per hertz above 110%, a measured current above In SF and a measured current below 50% of In (the load share is then overstated).

Rejections of an odd or out-of-range pole count and of a rated speed at or above the synchronous speed, and the shared range checks (positive output, voltage, frequency, current and speed, a power factor above 0 and up to 1, an efficiency above 0 and up to 100%, a service factor from 1 to 1.5).
notChecked: The insulation class, temperature rise, ambient and altitude derating, enclosure and IP rating, duty type, efficiency class and the other items printed on a plate that are set by IEC 60034 or NEMA MG 1: no standard table or clause is applied, and the locked-rotor ratio is entered, not decoded from a code letter or a kVA per horsepower table.

Single-phase, synchronous, DC and wound-rotor motors, a motor on a variable-frequency drive (use the VFD speed calculator), and a dual-voltage or dual-speed plate with more than one rating: enter one rating at a time.

The efficiency, power factor and temperature rise at the service-factor output and at part load, the effect of voltage or frequency variation on torque, slip and efficiency beyond the constant-output current estimate, voltage and current unbalance, harmonics, and the starting duty, the motor protection settings and the cable sizing that follow from the plate.

checked: A single circuit with one protective device: the kind of device (miniature, moulded-case or air circuit-breaker, or gG fuse link), the design current Ib, the cable current-carrying capacity Iz, the conventional operating factor k2 of the device, the prospective fault current Isc, the rated breaking capacity of the device to be used, the smallest fault current at the far end, the highest instantaneous trip setting as a multiple of the rating, the let-through energy I²t, the conductor area S and the adiabatic constant k.

The two-part overload condition In ≥ Ib and In ≤ Iz with k2 In ≤ 1.45 Iz (so In ≤ min(Iz, 1.45 Iz / k2)): the smallest standard rating at or above Ib from a common catalogue list for the kind of device (miniature 6 to 125 A, moulded-case 16 to 1,600 A, air circuit-breaker 630 to 6,300 A, gG fuse 2 to 1,250 A), the largest rating the cable allows, the loading Ib / In, the conventional operating current k2 In and its ratio to Iz, and whether any rating fits.

The smallest standard breaking capacity at or above Isc (3 to 150 kA list) and the ratio of the rated capacity of the device to Isc; the smallest end-of-circuit fault against the highest instantaneous trip m In (not made for a fuse); the cable withstand k² S² against the let-through I²t; and the number of checks not met.

Warnings for no standard rating between the load and the cable limit, a breaking capacity below the fault current, a fault current above 150 kA, a smallest fault below the highest trip setting, a let-through above the cable withstand, and a smallest fault larger than the prospective fault. Rejections of a design current above the largest rating in the list for the kind of device and of ranges outside the shared limits (a factor k2 of 1 to 3, positive currents).
notChecked: Any rule of an installation code or product standard beyond the textbook two-part condition: the 1.45 and k2 figures, the rating lists, the breaking capacity steps, the instantaneous trip bands and the adiabatic constant are conventions or the user's data-sheet figures and are not drawn from a licensed edition of IEC 60364-4-43, IEC 60898-1, IEC 60947-2 or IEC 60269.

Discrimination (selectivity) and back-up protection between devices in series, the voltage and pole rating, ambient temperature derating of the device, motor starting and transformer inrush, earth-fault loop impedance and the disconnection time on a time-current curve, arc-flash energy, and the energy let-through curve itself (the I²t is entered, not looked up).

Circuits with several devices, adjustable thermal and long-time settings, electronic trip units and short-time delay, direct current, and fuse time-current curves: the check is one rating and one set of fault figures.

checked: One measurement with a result that is a single reading or the mean of n readings: the measured value x, the sample standard deviation s of the readings and their number n (the Type A source, uA = s / √n with n − 1 degrees of freedom), up to four other sources each given as a standard uncertainty, a rectangular, triangular or U-shaped limit, an expanded uncertainty at k = 2 or a resolution step, and a sensitivity coefficient for each.

Each source converted to a standard uncertainty by its divisor (1, √3, √6, √2, 2 or 2√3), weighted by |c|, and combined as a root sum of squares into the combined standard uncertainty; the share of each source in the variance and the largest contributor.

The effective degrees of freedom by the Welch–Satterthwaite formula with the Type B sources taken as infinite, truncated to a whole number (one million or more taken as infinite); the coverage factor k = 2, k = 3 or a Student t factor for 95% or 99%; the expanded uncertainty U = k uc, the interval x ± U, U as a percentage of the reading and the test uncertainty ratio T / U.

Warnings for one source supplying 80% or more of the variance, a standard deviation from fewer than 3 readings, k = 2 or 3 with fewer than 30 effective degrees of freedom, a test uncertainty ratio below 4 and an expanded uncertainty above the tolerance. Rejections of a fractional number of readings, a standard deviation with fewer than 2 readings, a budget with no source, and a negative source value.
notChecked: Any clause of JCGM 100 (the GUM), JCGM 101, ISO/IEC 17025 or a laboratory accreditation rule: the method is the textbook root-sum-square budget on the figures the user enters, and no licensed text was reviewed.

Correlation between sources, a measurand that is a non-linear function of several inputs (the sensitivity coefficients are entered, not derived), Type B sources with a finite degrees of freedom, distributions other than the six listed, and the Monte Carlo method.

Correction of known systematic errors (the value x is taken as already corrected), the choice of the sources and the size of the figures you enter, traceability of the reference, a guard band or decision rule for a pass or fail against the tolerance, and the reporting rules of a calibration certificate.

checked: The group arithmetic on the figures the user enters: for each of two charger groups the connected load number × rated power / efficiency, the chargers in use as the share in use rounded up to a whole charger, and the demand in use × rated power × average power share / efficiency; the group and total connected load, the charger demand and the diversity factor (demand over connected load).

Power factor handled as P and Q for the chargers and for the building load (Q = P tan(arccos pf)): site kW, kvar, kVA, power factor and current (S / (√3 V) three-phase, S / V single-phase) at the peak, and the same with the spare-capacity percentage as the design demand and design current.
The next standard transformer at or above the design demand from the common size list (25 to 3,150 kVA) and the peak loading of it.

An optional supply limit in kVA: room under it at the peak and at the design demand, the charger kW the limit leaves after the building load (the root of √((P + Pb)² + (P tan φ + Qb)²) = limit), and the share of its rating each charger gets if every charger is used at once at full rating.

Warnings for a peak or design demand above the supply limit, every charger at once above what the limit leaves, the building load alone reaching the limit, a share in use below 40%, a charger power factor below 0.9, a large single-phase current, and a design demand above the largest standard transformer. Rejections of no charger in either group, a fractional number of chargers, a zero rating for a group with chargers, and values outside the shared ranges.
notChecked: Any clause of IEC 60364-7-722, IEC 61851-1, IEC 61439-7, NEC Article 625 or a local rule on EV supply demand, diversity or load management: the share in use, the average power and the efficiency are the user's judgement and no code demand or diversity table is applied. No licensed clause text was reviewed.

A utility connection rule, a maximum-demand tariff, a charge-session or arrival model, a load profile over the day, time-of-use control or an energy cost: demand is taken at one busiest moment and the building maximum demand is added in full.

Load-management or smart-charging controller design, the per-vehicle taper, vehicles that take less than their share, vehicle-to-grid export, harmonics, phase unbalance, inrush, voltage drop and cable or protection sizing for each charger.

checked: The battery arithmetic on the figures the user enters: for up to four load groups the average load Σ connected power × share drawn, the design load with the growth margin, the power from the battery after the efficiency, the bus current (power ÷ bus voltage), the ampere-hours taken over the backup time and the energy in kWh, and the current with every group at full power.

The nameplate capacity: ampere-hours taken divided by the usable fraction (depth of discharge × end-of-life capacity × low-temperature factor), the same in kWh, the first size at or above it in the list 50 to 2,000 Ah, and the full-power battery current as a multiple of that size (C).

The charger current to recharge in a set time: ampere-hours taken ÷ (recharge time × charge efficiency) plus the load current at the bus, and its power at the bus voltage; and, for an installed capacity, the runtime installed Ah × usable fraction ÷ average current and its margin over the backup time.

Warnings for an installed battery that is short of the backup time, a capacity above the largest listed size, a full-power discharge above 0.5 C, a depth of discharge above 80%, a backup time below 1 hour and a converter efficiency below 80%. Rejections of no load group with a power and a share above 0, and values outside the shared ranges.
notChecked: Any clause of EN 50129, EN 50155, EN 50122, EN 50160, IEC 60896, IEC 62485-2 or a national railway signalling or telecom power rule: the backup time, the loads and the three capacity allowances are the user's inputs, and no licensed clause text was reviewed. The calculator does not decide which loads are safety-related or what autonomy a railway operator requires.

A load profile over the outage, the short peaks of point machines, lamp proving, level-crossing barriers and other motors, the voltage falling towards the end of discharge and the end-of-discharge voltage the loads accept, Peukert or discharge-rate correction, battery chemistry, ageing curves, temperature over the year and cell balancing.

The charger float voltage, charge profile and current limit, the rectifier or UPS design, battery string and cable sizing, protection, ventilation of the battery room, and the cost, weight or space of the battery.

checked: The IEC 61724-1 energy ratio on the figures the user enters: the final yield Yf = E / P0 from the AC energy at the meter and the nameplate DC power, the reference yield Yr = H / 1 kW/m² from the plane-of-array irradiation, PR = Yf / Yr, the ideal energy P0 × H and the energy lost against it, and the daily final yield.
A temperature-corrected PR, PR / (1 + γ (Tm − 25)), from one average module temperature and a linear power coefficient.

A seven-step loss waterfall applied one step after another to the energy left by the step before (degradation (1 − d)^years, module temperature, soiling, DC wiring and mismatch, availability and curtailment, other losses, inverter efficiency): the kWh lost at each step, the expected energy, the expected PR (and the PR when new), the gap between the expected and the metered energy in kWh and per cent, and a check against a target PR giving the energy at the target, the shortfall and the margin in points.

Warnings for a PR above 100% or above 95%, below 60%, irradiation above 10 kWh/m² per day, a period under 7 days, a corrected PR above 100%, a module colder than 25 °C, a measured energy more than 5% below or 3% above the waterfall, and a PR below the target. Rejections of a positive temperature coefficient, and zero or negative energy, array power, irradiation or days (shared range checks).
notChecked: Any clause of IEC 61724-1, IEC 61724-2 or IEC 62446-3, or a contract acceptance protocol: the PR is the plain energy ratio on the entered figures, and no licensed text was reviewed. The monitoring class, sensor calibration and uncertainty, data filtering, measurement interval and test period are not checked.

The interval-by-interval temperature-weighted correction of IEC 61724-1 (one average module temperature is used), the temperature of the cell as distinct from the module back, and any irradiance-dependent efficiency.

Inverter clipping, trackers, bifacial gain, snow, grid availability data, sensor drift, a soiling model and first-year light-induced degradation as a separate step: every loss, the inverter efficiency and the annual degradation are the user's figures, and the order of the waterfall affects the kWh given to each step.
